page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-16 is a high-memory general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the processor operates with two threads per core and incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Vector extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), and AVX-VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 126.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.88 GB per vCPU, and contains no local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread execution efficiency paired with stable multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance ranks in the top tier, reflected in a stress-ng score of 3,457.67 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2,575.0. Single-threaded decompression and compression metrics are equally high, reaching 37.97 GB/sec in gzip compression and 16.92 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as the stress-ng multi-core score (27,645.75), PassMark CPU score (31,722.29), and Geekbench multi-core score (15,134.0) fall within the middle 50% range, reflecting its 8-core physical limit.

Memory throughput registers at 50.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 33.92 GB/sec for uncached writes, while cached small-block reads reach 1,675.53 GB/sec. Lightweight AI inference exhibits strong efficiency, reaching 2,787.22 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 406.36 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M parameter model. Scaled to a medium 7B model, processing settles into average ranges with 60.16 prompt tokens/sec and 12.43 generation tokens/sec. Operational throughput maintains 28.43 million Redis SET operations per second and 29.25 GB/sec in static web serving.

By delivering an expanded memory pool without demanding high core counts, the c4d-highmem-16 achieves favorable resource balance for memory-intensive architectures. However, deployments requiring local high-speed scratch disks will need network-attached storage solutions, as no local NVMe drives are included. This makes the instance appropriate for enterprise databases, in-memory caching tiers, large-footprint Java enterprise services, and memory-constrained data transformation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-16 is a memory-oriented server configured with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 x86_64 processor and 126.0 GB of memory. It features top-tier single-core compute performance, as shown by strong Geekbench and stress-ng results, combined with vector optimizations via AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI. The system contains no bundled GPU hardware and relies entirely on external storage. Multi-core compute and uncached memory bandwidth show average throughput relative to its core count, while small-model LLM inference and in-memory key-value operations perform reliably. The high RAM-to-vCPU ratio of roughly 7.88 GB per vCPU renders it cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial working memory without scaling processor allocation unnecessarily, making it suitable for in-memory databases, Redis caches, and data processing tasks.
